cases.sourceFinding: DailyPlannings is a date-keyed operating snapshot (groups, member-linked attendee drinks/requests, optional sessionId, versions); sessions is the separate confirmed record. Meeting start reads both in one transaction, archives an existing planning, updates only assigned attendees, rewrites/merges the planning and creates the session only if absent. renameDailyPlanningGroup reads current planning and linked session in a transaction and maps each current groups array, replacing only the target group's name; it preserves independently recorded games, notes, members and other groups and never recreates a group removed from the session. A valid missing linked session aborts before writes; invalid legacy links leave planning editable. Session deletion queries all matching planning links, removes only sessionId and deletes/audits the session in one batch. Version restoration uses the current sessionId rather than the archived snapshot link, so a detached deleted link is not revived. Planning deletion removes operating snapshot/versions while retaining the session.

cases.sourceFinding: The public /interview/:token path uses an exact interviewAccess bearer-token document. Public clients may get an active token (a missing token may also be fetched for invalid-link UX), cannot list/create/delete tokens or access internal interview collections, and may only update firstAccessedAt once or whitelisted response fields with server timestamps, active survey window, unique allowed slots and completed-interview lock. Active public schedules/rounds are get-readable and not listable to public users; rules do not require proof of token possession when reading an active public config. Admin authorization requires signed-in token.email and an admins document; stored master role or the bootstrap email permits master administration. Client normalizes email for its lookup. Current rules do not check email_verified. InterviewApplicant/InterviewAccess scheduleId optional string|null represents undefined legacy round, explicit null unassigned and ID assigned schedule. Public subscription stops at null, uses interviewPublicRounds on undefined, or schedule plus common-round subscription on ID. Public UI blocks null, permits fixed schedules during initialization, and holds legacy rolling-window initialization. Legacy schedule migration only accepts undefined and writes explicit schedule linkage. Rules accessScheduleId intentionally normalizes non-string/absent/null to null for legacy fallback. KST first-access plus four-day selection is calculated client-side; rules enforce the wider config slot subset, not that personal calendar window.
